text: For a given segment of a circle, to complete the circle, the very one of which it is a segment. Let $ABC$ be the given segment of a circle. So it is required to complete the circle for segment $ABC$, the very one of which it is a segment.
For let $AC$ be cut in half at (point) $D$ [Prop.~1.10],
and let $DB$ be drawn from point $D$, at right-angles to $AC$ [Prop.~1.11].
And let $AB$ be joined.
Thus, angle $ABD$ is surely either greater than, equal to, or less than (angle) $BAD$.
assertion: angle ABD is either greater than, equal to, or less than angle BAD (trichotomy)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $ABD$ is surely either greater than, equal to, or less than (angle) $BAD$

text: First of all, let it be greater.
assertion: angle ABD is greater than angle BAD (Case 1 hypothesis)

text: And let (angle) $BAE$, equal to angle $ABD$, be constructed on the straight-line $BA$, at the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.23].
And let $DB$ be drawn through to $E$,
and let $EC$ be joined.
Therefore, since angle $ABE$ is equal to $BAE$, the straight-line $EB$ is thus also equal to $EA$ [Prop.~1.6].
And since $AD$ is equal to $DC$, and $DE$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AD$, $DE$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CD$, $DE$, respectively.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: two (straight-lines) $AD$, $DE$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CD$, $DE$, respectively

text: And angle $ADE$ is equal to angle $CDE$. For each (is) a right-angle.
Thus, the base $AE$ is equal to the base $CE$ [Prop.~1.4].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: base $AE$ is equal to the base $CE$

text: But, $AE$ was shown (to be) equal to $BE$.
Thus, $BE$ is also equal to $CE$.
Thus, the three (straight-lines) $AE$, $EB$, and $EC$ are equal to one another.
assertion: AE, EB, EC are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: three (straight-lines) $AE$, $EB$, and $EC$ are equal to one another

text: Thus, if a circle is drawn with center $E$, and radius one of $AE$, $EB$, or $EC$, it will also go through the remaining points (of the segment), and the (associated circle) will be completed [Prop.~3.9].
assertion: the circle with center E and radius AE/EB/EC passes through remaining segment points and completes the circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: if a circle is drawn with center $E$, and radius one of $AE$, $EB$, or $EC$, it will also go through the remaining points (of the segment), and the (associated circle) will be completed

text: Thus, a circle has been completed from the given segment of a circle.
assertion: a circle has been completed from the given segment (Case 1 result)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a circle has been completed from the given segment of a circle

text: And (it is) clear that the segment $ABC$ is less than a semi-circle, because the center $E$ happens to lie outside it.
assertion: segment ABC is less than a semi-circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: segment $ABC$ is less than a semi-circle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: because the center $E$ happens to lie outside it

text: [And], similarly, even if angle $ABD$ is equal to $BAD$, (since) $AD$ becomes equal to each of $BD$ [Prop.~1.6] and $DC$, the three (straight-lines) $DA$, $DB$, and $DC$ will be equal to one another.
assertion: DA, DB, DC are equal to one another (Case 2)

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $AD$ becomes equal to each of $BD$ [Prop.~1.6] and $DC$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: three (straight-lines) $DA$, $DB$, and $DC$ will be equal to one another

text: And point $D$ will be the center of the completed circle.
assertion: D is the center of the completed circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: point $D$ will be the center of the completed circle

text: And $ABC$ will manifestly be a semi-circle.

And if $ABD$ is less than $BAD$, and we construct (angle $BAE$), equal to angle $ABD$, on the straight-line $BA$, at the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.23], then the center will fall on $DB$, inside the segment $ABC$.
assertion: the center falls on DB, inside segment ABC (Case 3)

spans.label: glue
spans.text: , and we construct (angle $BAE$), equal to angle $ABD$, on the straight-line $BA$, at the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.23], then the

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: center will fall on $DB$, inside the segment $ABC$

text: And segment $ABC$ will manifestly be greater than a semi-circle.
assertion: segment ABC is greater than a semi-circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: segment $ABC$ will manifestly be greater than a semi-circle

text: Thus, a circle has been completed from the given segment of a circle. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
